history.value: Andreessen Horowitz was founded in 2009 by Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz on the belief that software would eat the world, starting with a $300M fund. Early bets on Facebook, Instagram, GitHub, Slack, Airbnb and Coinbase made its name. It now manages over $100B, with separate funds for AI, crypto, bio and health, games and American industry.

The base-tag recompute is guarded off as unrepresentative: only 251 of 1,807 base rows carry a sector tag, all from the speedrun accelerator surface, so a recomputed focus would describe 14% of the portfolio (accelerator-skewed) rather than the firm; the crosswalk for those tags is staged in config.json and the recompute publishes automatically if tag coverage ever reaches 25% of the base.

investment_range.basis: Median: partner-anchored entry-round median $24,734,937 across 182 membership-verified base companies with priced Form D histories (594 rounds; 72 entries anchored past pre-investor rounds), published as $25M. p10 $2.2M, p25 $11.8M, p75 $50.0M, p90 $100.0M. Pre-base corroboration: $30.0M over the 93 investment-list-confirmed issuers of the roster sweep. A round-size proxy for check size, fair for a high-ownership lead investor. | Lower limit: speedrun accelerator checks, $500K upfront (up to $1M per company), the program floor. | Upper limit: the $2B Thinking Machines Lab seed round led by a16z, July 2025 (a16z share undisclosed; Nvidia, AMD, Accel, Jane Street in the consortium; news.crunchbase.com/venture/biggest-seed-round-ai-thinking-machines-mira-murati/). Dry-powder check: the $6.75B Growth Fund V at a 10-15% single-position concentration supports $675M-$1B positions; the $2B ceiling is the led-round figure, not a single-check claim | UPPER LIMIT CORRECTED 2026-10-09 (quantitative QA, Erik): $1.0B, 15% of the $6.75B largest fund, the single-position cap of COLLECTION.md 11. The $2B Thinking Machines Lab seed is a round size with a16z's share undisclosed and is rejected as a range end.

individuals.basis: Live team payload: 103 members, the site's own Investment Team (96) and Board Partners (7) groups; 469 Operations Team members excluded by the flagged scope decision. Positions are the site's own flat presentation: every investing member renders 'Partner' (cofounders included), Board Partners carry the group's own label. The roster is the current site team by design (Wayback CDX was offline this run), so the departed cross-check is structurally empty; the alumni limitation is recorded in report.md. Social links: 93 of 103 people carry a LinkedIn or X link (77 LinkedIn, 68 X): 135 carried from an earlier read of the site; 10 from a checked search whose result names both the person and the firm. 10 without a link.

flags.note: Scope decision: the site's own Investment Team (96) and Board Partners (7) groups only, 103 people; the 469 Operations Team members (marketing, finance, legal, talent, GTM network) are excluded from the published list — a16z staffs ~5x the investing organization and the full 572 would swamp the surface. The site presents every investing member as 'Partner' (page-title template), including the cofounders; Board Partners carry the group's own label. Wayback CDX was unavailable 2026-08-29, so the historical-roster departed cross-check is empty pending the PRO-30 roster run.

Post-2022 restructure: LP capital enters through AH Annual Fund / Fund Multiplexer conduit vehicles, so strategy-fund Form Ds understate raises (Crypto 4 $4.5B and Crypto V $2.2B are press figures; Growth IV/V, Infra, Apps, American Dynamism, Bio+Health 2026 and both Games funds are announced allocations). Where press and filing disagree the filed amount is published (LSV II $3.0B vs press $3.2B; Fund VII $1.25B vs press $1.3B). The $3B 'other venture strategies' leg of the January 2026 raise (Fund X - AI Applications / AI Infrastructure vehicles on EDGAR) is not yet listed as a fund pending a named size.

RAUM ($106.48B, 2026-03-30) is gross regulatory assets and can overstate net AUM; the bottom is the firm's own 'over $100B+' claim (about page, 2026-04-30). The $1.1B Machine Age Fund (2026-08-28) postdates both. a16z Perennial Management (CRD 324429), the separately registered private-wealth/evergreen adviser, is excluded from both AUM and the fund list.

Median recomputed on the final base (2026-08-29): $24.7M over 182 verified companies, vs $30.0M on the pre-base list-confirmed subset. Priced Form D rounds only — speedrun SAFEs and 4(a)(2) raises don't file, so the small end is under-sampled. A few distribution tails ride on weak CIK joins (e.g. slug 'dynamic' at $1.1B); PRO-31's standing weak-CIK audit is the cleanup pass, and the median is insensitive to them. The $2B ceiling is the led-round figure for the Thinking Machines seed (a16z's own share undisclosed), consistent with the $6.75B Growth Fund V's concentration capacity.

The firm publishes Seed / Venture / Growth filters; splitting 'Venture' into Series A + Series B is this run's interpretation. Late Stage rests on the firm's own Late Stage Venture (LSV) fund family; Pre-Seed on speedrun's stated 'pre-seed or seed' scope.

Core US is unambiguous. 'Other' is inferred: Europe and Israel from named companies on the firm's own investment list, Asia from the Seoul and Tokyo offices — no firm statement enumerates its geographies. Verify or trim in review.

Asserted two ways: against the firm's own portfolio page/investment list during the base-less run, and against auto_confirmed base rows by build-firm-profile.py once the PRO-30 base landed (2026-08-29) — all eight pass both.

Base-tag focus recompute guarded off: only the 251 speedrun rows of 1,807 carry sector tags, so the firm's own nine-sector enumeration stands (crosswalk for the speedrun vocabulary staged in config.json). Separately, four of the nine focus values (Crypto & Web3, Healthcare & Bio, Consumer & Marketplaces, Media Gaming & Advertising) are among the five values added to the taxonomy 2026-08-13; the DB migration and leaderboard filter update for investor-side focus are tracked separately, so those labels pass the taxonomy gate but do not filter on the frontend yet.
